questions.question: Compute ∫ x² dx.
questions.rationale: The power rule raises the exponent by one and divides by the new power: ∫x² dx = x³/3 + C.

questions.question: What is ∫ 1/x dx?
questions.rationale: The power n = −1 would divide by zero, so it is the exception: 1/x integrates to the natural logarithm, ln ∣x∣ + C, since d/dx of ln ∣x∣ is 1/x.

questions.question: Compute ∫ (3x² + 4x − 5) dx.
questions.rationale: Integrate term by term: 3x² gives x³, 4x gives 2x², −5 gives −5x — sum rule and constant multiple rule — so the answer is x³ + 2x² − 5x + C.

questions.question: Evaluate the definite integral of x² from x = 0 to x = 2.
questions.rationale: The antiderivative is x³/3, and the fundamental theorem gives F(2) − F(0) = 8/3 − 0 = 8/3 ≈ 2.67 square units of area.

questions.question: Why does every indefinite integral end with + C?
options: It marks the constant of the variable
Vertical shifts all share the same derivative, so integration cannot recover them
It is just a convention with no meaning
questions.rationale: x² + 1, x² − 7 and x² + π all differentiate to 2x — derivatives cannot see vertical shifts, so integration must report the whole family of curves.

questions.question: Which quantity does integrating velocity over a time interval directly give you?
questions.rationale: Integrating velocity gives displacement — signed, so backwards motion subtracts. Distance travelled requires integrating the speed |v(t)|.

questions.question: Which statement about definite integrals is TRUE?
options: They require the + C in the answer
They evaluate to a number: antiderivative at the top bound minus at the bottom
questions.rationale: The fundamental theorem of calculus turns a definite integral into F(b) − F(a): a single number. The + C cancels in the subtraction, and regions below the x-axis count negative.

questions.question: Compute ∫ 2x(x² + 1)³ dx using substitution.
questions.rationale: Let u = x² + 1 so du = 2x dx; the integral becomes ∫u³ du = u⁴/4 + C = (x² + 1)⁴/4 + C — differentiating confirms it returns the integrand.

questions.question: Which technique handles integrals of products like x·sin x?
questions.rationale: Products of unlike functions need integration by parts, which moves the derivative from one factor to the other; substitution works for chain-rule-shaped integrands like 2x(x² + 1)³.

questions.question: An economist knows a firm's marginal cost. Which integration application recovers total cost?
options: Multiply by the number of workers
questions.rationale: Every 'total from a rate' question is an integral in disguise — integrating the marginal (rate of change) function accumulates it back into the total.
